gaps.fact: Aurore, one of the Court's two named hybrids, appears nowhere in the Codex; Seyval Blanc is taught and asked.
Gewürztraminer as a New York white: it is listed only among the finger-lakes article's grapes and the country record's; no chapter names it for New York and no question asks it.

Mould in the humid New York summer, the second half of the Court's cell: only the long-island article teaches it (mildew and botrytis, card 6); neither chapter mentions disease pressure in New York and no question asks it.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 61 (United States, of which 5 are New York: i-59liyzk3, i-iklks4f7, i-xci1ziz8, i-mqovf1a4, i-6hle0w8z) and Village 33 (Pacific NW, NY & Canada, of which 7 are New York: c-y9kh51ed, c-f28qgard, c-r1i04gcg, c-0mqtty1y, c-7gg379fv, c-jh8sw72q, c-ogj6yymb), 94 in all, 12 of them New York. A small subject and well held: the lake effect, the three families of vine, Frank's rootstock argument, Finger Lakes Riesling, Long Island's maritime Merlot and the labrusca rules are all taught and asked. The Certified AVAs are uneven: Long Island is asked twice, while the Hudson River Region and Lake Erie rest on one chapter sentence each and on region questions outside both banks, so a bank question on each would be worth writing although the rule here does not count them as gaps. The real gaps are Aurore, which nothing names, Gewürztraminer in New York, and the summer mould. No error found: Cayuga Lake 1988 as the first nested AVA, Seneca the deepest, Keuka's Y and Hammondsport, the 51 per cent labrusca minimum and Lake Erie as the largest planting all hold. One search spent, on New York AVA rules since 8.2023: none found (the last New York AVA was Upper Hudson in 2018), so courtUpdates is empty.
